citations.title: Purpose and scope
citations.requirement: Chapter sets minimum requirements for residential services to people with DD. It applies to provider-managed group homes and supervised apartments. Community care residences (Family Care/Skill Development in a private home) are licensed under 10:44B. Head-injury residences fall under 10:44C. Licensing is voluntary where no resident needs personal guidance, as decided by the planning team.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines the terms the manual must use. Community residence: up to 16 individuals, not on the grounds of or immediately adjacent to public institutions serving a similar population. Supervised apartment: up to 4 individuals per apartment. Full license: up to one year. Also defines Abuse, Exploitation, Central Registry, Critical information, Direct support professional, Governing authority, Community agency head, Executive director, Behavior support plan, Falsification, Fiduciary capacity, Guardian, Authorization to operate (permits operation past license expiration when an inspection is delayed), Eviction, and Service plan/planning team.

citations.title: Application for licensure
citations.requirement: (a) Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider plus the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider. (b) No agency head may be paid or contracted until criminal history clearance under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-63 through 69; owner/licensee also checked if different from the agency head. (c)(1) Application contents include a table of organization, CVs, owners, 24 months of service history with survey results and plans of correction, penalties/fines record, CPA examination for two fiscal years, and 3 professional references each. (d)(1) 45 days to complete or the application may be denied, with a 6-month bar on reapplying. (g) Written decision within 60 calendar days. (i) The procedure manual goes to the Office of Licensing before opening, then job descriptions go to DDD. (j) No operation without Office of Licensing authorization. (k) DHS inspection without limitation or notice. (l) Annual on-site inspection. (m) No license after denial by any State agency for substantial noncompliance. (n) No license if a final finding of discrimination exists.

citations.title: General requirements
citations.requirement: (a) The licensee's purposes and a description of its services must be made available to individuals, parents, guardians, advocates and the general public. Other subsections of 2.1 were not read.

citations.title: Development and maintenance of procedure manual
citations.requirement: (a) Licensee develops and implements a written procedure manual. Procedures are reviewed annually. Each procedure is designed on normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning. Each has a unique title, purpose, sequential steps, staff responsibilities and reporting/recording requirements. (b) Required contents: 1 philosophy; 2 table of organization; 3 Central Registry compliance; 4 New Employee Orientation Checklist; 5 major emergency/evacuation plan, including indoor air below 68F or above 82F for four consecutive hours; 6 medical emergencies with a 9-1-1 call for life-threatening emergencies (Danielle's Law, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-5.1 et seq.; N.J.A.C. 10:42A); 7 emergency coverage/on-call; 8 unusual incident reporting with a written prohibition on abuse, neglect and exploitation and the obligation to report each allegation; 9 investigations; 10 fiscal management of personal funds; 11 safekeeping of valuables; 12 list and schedule of charges and fees; 13 complaint/grievance procedure with at least two levels, the last involving the licensee or executive director; 14 separate internal communication/critical-information log; 15 admissions per 10:44A-4; 16 confidentiality per N.J.A.C. 10:41-2; 17 medication administration and self-medication; 18 controlled dangerous substance testing of employees (N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5); 19 exchange of contact information with involved family/guardians (N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6); 20 Child Abuse Registry check; 21 video/audio monitoring of common areas, if applicable; 22 continuous quality improvement system.

citations.title: Implementation of procedure manual
citations.requirement: The section exists per the LII subchapter 2 table of contents. Its operative text was not read. Confirm what it requires for staff access to and implementation of the manual before relying on it.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Personnel requirements, including employee screening. All employees who may contact individuals must comply with the screening requirements. A provider-hosted copy of the 2023 text shows a TB screen (Mantoux 5 TU PPD or IGRA blood test) within one year before or upon starting work, with written results submitted to the licensee. The 2005 text also required annual repeat testing, so confirm the current subsection letter and any repeat interval.

citations.title: Minimum staff qualifications
citations.requirement: (a) Licensee or executive director has a bachelor's degree, five years of progressive DD management experience (at least two supervisory at a senior/administrative level), and knowledge of program design, staff development and fiscal/qualitative standards. (b) Residence supervisor has a high school diploma or equivalent plus one year of DD experience. (c) DSPs are 18 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent. (d) DSPs can communicate with the individuals they work with. (e) DSPs can provide the direct assistance or training required. (f) Licensee verifies professional credentials required by law for employed or contracted professionals.

citations.title: Orientation
citations.requirement: The section exists per the LII table of contents. 10:44A-2.2(b)4 requires the New Employee Orientation Checklist to include all of 10:44A-2.6(a)1 through 8. The text of 2.6 was not read, so confirm the eight items before drafting the checklist.

citations.title: Staff training
citations.requirement: (a) Within 90 days of employment each DSP completes Division basic training: DDD Shifting Expectations, preventing abuse and neglect, first aid and CPR from an ECC-compliant entity, each with a valid certificate on file. (b) Medication training and demonstrated competency come before administering any medication, and competency is shown annually. (c) Training in all relevant policies not covered in orientation. (d) Specialized training within 90 days of employment: feeding techniques (feeding tube duties delegated to nursing), mobility devices and transport, seizure/physical/medical needs, mental health needs, and behavior support plans. (e) Training records kept in the administrative office with a curriculum/training plan, dated trainer and trainee signatures, and Division-required results. (f) Additional training is allowed without Division approval. (g) Training under (c) is delivered by a qualified trainer.

citations.title: Staff coverage
citations.requirement: (a) A written staff schedule for at least two weeks is available at each residence with full staff names. It shows on-site coverage per the program description, and an in-charge employee for each shift. Temporary agency staff may not be designated in-charge unless all 2.7 training is complete and a written policy states the licensee assumes responsibility and liability. (b) Each required specialized training is completed by at least one person on each shift. (c) Staff need not be on site when no individuals are present, but trained, paid agency staff familiar with the individuals must be available for emergencies. (d) Group home/supervised apartment staff are on site whenever any individual is present, per supervision needs. (e) The staff residence/office of a supervised apartment program is located so response time fits supervision needs. No numeric ratio or awake-overnight rule was found in 10:44A.

citations.title: Records of individuals receiving services
citations.requirement: (a) An individual file is kept for each individual receiving services. (b) Files for group home and supervised apartment residents are kept at the residence. Contents include full name, DOB and sex; Social Security and Medicaid/insurance numbers; and dates of admission, readmission, transfer or discharge. The remaining required contents and any retention period were not read.

citations.title: Individual financial records: personal funds
citations.requirement: The licensee keeps a written record of all financial arrangements and transactions involving individuals' entrusted funds. Each individual and guardian has access to it on request, and copies are provided on request. The 2005 text also required the licensee to manage funds so as not to jeopardize benefit entitlements. Confirm the current subsection.

citations.title: Advocacy and rights: General requirements
citations.requirement: (a) Services recognize that people with disabilities have the same rights as other citizens, and exercising rights is never a cause for retribution. (b) Licensee complies with the Developmentally Disabled Rights Act, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-1 et seq. (c) Staff are familiar with and observe the rights listed in the Division's rights document. The licensee provides the rights document and gets acknowledgments on admission. (d) Individuals receive training and support to understand options, make choices and exercise rights. Rights are not limited because an individual has a guardian or family. (e) The licensee uses a Human Rights Committee under N.J.A.C. 10:41A. House rules involve the affected individuals, are necessary for order, and do not infringe on others' rights.

citations.title: Rules governing a residence
citations.requirement: Title seen in the 2005 rule text and the 2023 subchapter 3 range (3.1 to 3.3). Snippets show house rules must involve the affected individuals, be necessary to promote order, and not infringe on others' rights. The current text was not read, so confirm subsection lettering.

citations.title: Self-advocacy
citations.requirement: Title seen only in the 2005 rule text. The current operative text was not read. Confirm what it requires for supporting self-advocacy before relying on it.

citations.title: Pre-admission and admission
citations.requirement: Title seen in the 2005 rule text and in the 2023 subchapter 4 range (4.1 to 4.3). 10:44A-2.2(b)15 requires the admission procedure to comply with 10:44A-4. The operative text was not read. Confirm pre-admission and admission steps from the current text.

citations.title: Changes in supports/services
citations.requirement: Title seen in the 2005 rule text and the 2023 subchapter range. The operative text, including any transfer/discharge notice rules, was not read. Confirm before use.

citations.title: Individual Habilitation Plan (IHP)
citations.requirement: (a) The licensee has and implements a procedure for developing, implementing, reviewing and evaluating each individual's habilitation or service plan under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-10 et seq. (b) The plan and monthly documentation of progress are kept in the individual's record. (c) The comprehensive IHP includes 14 elements: cover page; evaluation summaries; progress on prior goals; preferences, capabilities and needs; goals; measurable sequential objectives; method for each objective; team members and responsible persons; services with start dates, duration and frequency; barriers; guardianship review; meeting summary/addendum (disagreement may be noted); attendance sign-off; and authorization for approved individual expenses.

citations.title: Subchapter 5 - Health and Safety
citations.requirement: The subchapter spans 10:44A-5.1 to 5.8 per the LII table of contents. A DHS 2/14/2023 webinar says 5.1(g)8-9 added a CPR mask and protective gloves to first aid kit requirements. The 2005 text had 5.1 General health care and 5.3 Over-the-counter medications. The rest of the subchapter text was not read, so confirm each section number and requirement (health care, OTC medications, food/diets, restraint/behavioral supports, incident rules) before citing it individually.

citations.title: Prescription medication
citations.requirement: (a) Individuals self-administer to the extent possible, as determined by the planning team, documented in the record and following licensee procedure. (b) If the individual cannot, the licensee or designee assists and supervises administration as prescribed. (c) A record is kept of all medication administered, including individual's name, date and medication name. For PRN medication the label must show name, date, medication, dosage, interval, maximum amount per 24 hours, stop date where appropriate, and conditions for giving it. An Advanced Practice Nurse may prescribe (2023 amendment).

citations.title: Subchapter 6 - Fire Safety and Physical Environment
citations.requirement: The subchapter spans 6.1 to 6.17 per the LII table of contents. Rule text seen indicates the licensee must obtain documentation of any required Fire Official inspection and registration with the Department of Community Affairs, and a certificate from the local enforcing authority (or documentation that none is issued). The individual section text, including drill frequency, was not read, so confirm each section number and requirement before citing it individually.

citations.title: Manual of Standards for Community Care Residences (scope exclusion)
citations.requirement: Owner-occupied Family Care/Skill Development living arrangements are licensed under 10:44B and not 10:44A. This manual covers provider-managed homes and apartments only.

citations.title: Notice of Readoption, N.J.A.C. 10:44A
citations.requirement: 10:44A was readopted effective February 17, 2026 (new expiration February 17, 2033). DHS stated further rulemaking may be necessary. The section text cited here is the 2023-amended text, so recheck against the current rule each year.

citations.title: Enhanced Human Services enforcement authority over developmental disability providers (Jan 2026)
citations.requirement: Expands DHS enforcement authority over DD providers. The statute text was not reviewed, so counsel should read the penalty provisions.

citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care/home health services. NJ applies it to DDD Individual Supports, In-Home Respite and Community Based Supports through HHAeXchange. A Live-In Worker Attestation allows exclusion where the worker lives with the person served.

citations.cite: NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration (Section 1115); HCBS Statewide Transition Plan Addendum #3
citations.title: Authority for DDD Supports Program / Community Care Program
citations.requirement: DDD services are authorized under the 1115 demonstration (no longer 1915(c) since Nov 2017). NJ's HCBS settings transition plan applies to 10:44A homes.

citations.cite: DDD - Apply to Become a Provider
citations.title: Combined Application / Individual Supports provider approval
citations.requirement: Agencies that want to run a licensed residential setting submit the Combined Application and select Individual Supports. At least 24 months of documented direct-care service history is required, including survey/audit results and plans of correction.

citations.title: Annual audit and Fiscal Sustainability Report
citations.requirement: An annual financial statement audit is required for agencies claiming $350,000 or more in combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement. The audit follows GAAS. The Fiscal Sustainability Report is due 120 days after the state fiscal year ends (about October 30).

citations.cite: DDD Division Update, January 22, 2026; iRecord Rate Change (1/1/2026)
citations.title: DSP/DSP Supervisor wage pass-through
citations.requirement: Rates for nine agency-provided services rose 1/1/2026. Agencies must pass through about $0.46/hr as a base-wage increase to DSPs and DSP Supervisors no later than 3/1/2026, with retroactive pay. It cannot be paid as a bonus or used for operating expenses.

citations.cite: NJ DHS Office of Licensing (OPIA) provider page
citations.title: Inspections, provisional licenses and enforcement posture
citations.requirement: Annual and unannounced inspections, which increase beginning 2026. Inspectors review staff files, schedules, credentials, background checks, physical plant and insurance documents. Partial compliance can produce a provisional license, and two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal. Housing must be cleared with DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development before acquisition.

citations.cite: DDD FFS FAQ: Becoming a Medicaid Provider
citations.title: Medicaid approval before billing
citations.requirement: An agency must be Medicaid-approved to submit claims for DDD services, and the same Combined Application is used for Medicaid and DDD approval. NJ Medicaid denies claims from providers without a Medicaid ID.

policies.title: Governing Authority, Licensee/Executive Director and Residence Supervisor Responsibilities
state_specifics: Terms: licensee, community agency head, executive director, governing authority, residence supervisor (10:44A-1.3).

Executive director/licensee: bachelor's degree, 5 years progressive DD management (2 supervisory at a senior level), and program/fiscal knowledge (2.5(a)). Residence supervisor: HS diploma/equivalent plus 1 year of DD experience (2.5(b)).
Manual must hold a philosophy statement and a table of organization with lines of authority (2.2(b)1-2).
Licensee must verify credentials of employed or contracted professionals (2.5(f)).
Purposes and a description of services must be available to individuals, parents, guardians, advocates and the public (2.1(a)).

policies.title: Licensure, Authorization to Operate and DDD/Medicaid Provider Approval
state_specifics: No one may own or operate a community residence without Office of Licensing authorization (1.4(j)), and individuals may not be placed before approval.

Application: Combined Application plus Attestation for Individual Supports Provider, with 24 months of service history. 45-day completeness window, 6-month reapplication bar, 60-calendar-day decision (1.4(d),(g)).
Full license is up to one year. Annual on-site inspection (1.4(l)). 'Authorization to operate' letter covers operation past expiry when an inspection is delayed (1.3).
Capacity: up to 16 per community residence; up to 4 per supervised apartment; siting not on or adjacent to public institution grounds (1.3).
Provisional license and non-renewal after two consecutive provisional licenses (OPIA).
Chapter readopted eff. 2/17/2026 (58 N.J.R. 1193(b)). Text cited is the 2023 amendment text, so confirm against current rule.
Falsification during the application is cause for denial (1.4(h)). Denial history and discrimination findings bar licensure (1.4(m),(n)). Scope exclusion: 10:44B (family care) is separate.

policies.title: Procedure Manual Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Procedures must be reviewed annually and revised as necessary (2.2(a)1).
Every procedure needs a unique descriptive title, purpose, sequential steps, staff responsibilities, and reporting/recording requirements (2.2(a)3).

New applicants submit the manual to the Office of Licensing for approval after application approval and before opening. Job descriptions then go to DDD for each table-of-organization position (1.4(i)).
Do not carry forward Office of Licensing contact details from the 2005 rule.

policies.title: Continuous Quality Improvement System and Incident/Mortality Review
state_specifics: CQI system required by 2.2(b)22 with five minimum elements: (i) written data collection/analysis plan to find patterns; (ii) input from individuals, families and others; (iii) written summary of satisfaction surveys; (iv) written summary of outcomes assessments; (v) action plan based on that analysis.

Office of Licensing may require an action plan and implementation results when process or systemic problems are identified. This is stated in 10:44C and likely mirrored in 10:44A, so confirm the section.
Mortality review is not a 10:44A-specified requirement. Treat it as an internal review that feeds CQI and the unusual-incident process.

policies.title: DDD/Medicaid Compliance, Fee-for-Service Billing and Service Documentation
state_specifics: Services are approved and paid through DDD as Individual Supports under the CCP/Supports Program (Section 1115), fee-for-service. Bill only after delivery, against DDD authorizations.
Medicaid ID must be active before any claim. Claims deny without it.
Reconcile claims to authorizations monthly. Rate/code questions go to DDD.FeeForService@dhs.nj.gov (email per DDD update, confirm).
Monthly documentation of progress is part of the record (4.3(b)). Billing must be supported by the daily and monthly documentation.
DSP/DSP Supervisor wage pass-through of about $0.46/hr, effective 1/1/2026, base wage only (not a bonus), with a 3/1/2026 deadline including retroactive pay.
Falsification of records is defined in 1.3 and is cause for adverse licensing action.

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification (EVV)
state_specifics: EVV applies to DDD Individual Supports, In-Home Respite and Community Based Supports. NJ's vendor is HHAeXchange. NJ went live 1/1/2021.
Live-In Worker Attestation applies only where the worker actually lives with the person served.

Procedure covers clock-in/out at point of service, exception handling and reconciliation before billing. Helpdesk email DDDEVV@dhs.nj.gov is unverified, so confirm it on the DDD EVV page. Confirm current compliance deadlines with DDD.

policies.title: Licensing Inspections, Deficiencies, Plans of Correction and Enforcement Readiness
state_specifics: Residences are subject to DHS inspection or investigation without limitation or notice, covering records, equipment, sanitary conditions, accommodations and management of individuals (1.4(k)). Annual on-site inspection (1.4(l)).
Unannounced inspections are increasing from 2026. Inspectors review staff files, schedules, credentials, background checks, physical plant and insurance documents.
A 'deficiency' means noncompliance with a rule in the chapter (1.3). Respond to citations in writing by the notice deadline.
P.L.2025, c.280 (Jan 2026) enhances DHS enforcement authority. Have counsel review penalty provisions.
Assign a host per residence and keep files inspection-ready.

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Individuals have the same rights as all citizens. Exercise of rights may never be prohibited or used for retribution (3.1(a)).
Comply with the Developmentally Disabled Rights Act, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-1 et seq. (3.1(b)).
Provide the Division's rights document and obtain acknowledgment on admission. Train staff on it (3.1(c)).
Train and support individuals to understand options, make choices and exercise rights. Rights are not limited because of a guardian or family (3.1(d)).
Self-advocacy support (3.3) and house-rule rules (3.2) are in the 2005 text, so confirm current wording.

HCBS settings elements (privacy, lockable bedroom doors, visitors, schedule control, access to food, community access) come from the federal rule and the STP. Confirm any NJ-specific wording in 10:44A-3 and 6.

policies.title: Rights Restrictions, House Rules and Due Process
state_specifics: House rules must be developed with the individuals affected, be necessary to promote order, and not infringe on others' rights or endanger others (3.1/3.2).
Any individual-specific restriction should be reviewed by the Human Rights Committee under N.J.A.C. 10:41A. Document the assessed need, the less restrictive alternatives tried, and the plan.
Planned behavioral interventions in an approved plan are not abuse or neglect (2005 definition). Confirm current subchapter 5 text before drafting restraint language.

policies.title: Human Rights Committee
state_specifics: Licensee is responsible for utilizing a Human Rights Committee in accordance with N.J.A.C. 10:41A (3.1(e)).
Maintain a roster, meeting minutes and review records. Confirm HRC membership/meeting requirements in N.J.A.C. 10:41A, which was not read.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Complaint/grievance procedure must have at least two levels of hearing, the last involving the licensee or the executive director (2.2(b)13). 2023 amendments modified the complaint/grievance language, so check the current text.
Document each complaint, the response and the outcome. Feed results into the CQI plan.
Retaliation for exercising rights is prohibited (3.1(a)1).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Manual must include a confidentiality statement per N.J.A.C. 10:41-2 (2.2(b)16).
Individual files for group homes and supervised apartments are kept at the residence (2.9(b)). Control access and storage there.
Staff-held shift communication logs are kept separate from individual records (2.2(b)14).
Video/audio monitoring in common areas needs its own procedure (2.2(b)21).
HIPAA applies if the agency is a covered entity (e.g., electronic Medicaid billing). Federal documentation retention is 6 years.

policies.title: Personal Funds and Property Management
state_specifics: Manual requires a procedure for sound fiscal management of individuals' personal funds (2.2(b)10) and for safekeeping of valuable personal possessions (2.2(b)11).
Licensee acts in a 'fiduciary capacity' (1.3).
Individual and guardian get access to the written record of all financial arrangements and transactions on request, with copies (2.10).
Manage funds so they do not jeopardize benefit entitlements (2005 text; confirm current).
Approved individual expenses are authorized in the IHP (4.3(c)14).
Exploitation (using an individual's resources for another's advantage) is defined in 1.3 and is reportable.

policies.title: Schedule of Charges and Fees
state_specifics: Manual must include a list and schedule of all charges and fees an individual is responsible for (2.2(b)12). Give it to the individual and guardian at admission and on change.
Room and board/SSI contribution rules were not verified. Confirm with DDD before setting any charge.
SSI federal benefit rate is $994/month in 2026 (benchmark only).

policies.title: Informed Consent and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: 'Guardian' means a court-appointed person or agency (1.3). Verify guardianship status at admission. The IHP includes a review of guardianship status (4.3(c)11).
Exercise of rights is not limited because there is a guardian or family (3.1). Support the individual to decide with the least restrictive supports.
Individuals may note disagreement with any part of the plan in the meeting summary/addendum (4.3(c)12).

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
state_specifics: No license is issued to or held by anyone found by a court of record or the Division on Civil Rights to have discriminated based on race, color, creed, gender, national origin, ancestry or disability (1.4(n)).
DSPs must be able to communicate with the individuals they work with (2.5(d)).
Provide language access, interpreter and alternate-format procedures for individuals, guardians and families, plus accommodation for hearing/vision/AAC needs.

policies.title: Exchange of Family and Guardian Contact Information
state_specifics: Written procedures for exchanging contact information with parents, actively involved family members or guardians who choose to participate (2.2(b)19, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6).
Record each person's opt-in or opt-out and keep contacts current.

policies.title: Video/Audio Monitoring in Common Areas (if used)
state_specifics: Required if monitoring is used in common areas of the residences (2.2(b)21).
Never in bedrooms or bathrooms (standard practice). Describe notice to individuals, guardians and staff, who can view and how long footage is kept, plus Human Rights Committee review.

policies.title: Referral, Pre-Admission and Admission
state_specifics: Admission procedure must comply with 10:44A-4 (2.2(b)15). Confirm 4.1 text.
Individuals are 21+ and Medicaid-eligible, referred through DDD and support coordination. Do not place anyone before the Office of Licensing approves the residence (license provisions).
Admission file captures name, DOB, sex, Social Security/Medicaid numbers and admission date (2.9(b)).
Occupancy must not exceed licensed capacity, which is stated on the license for each residence.

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning and the Individual Plan (IHP/Service Plan)
state_specifics: Written procedure for developing, implementing, reviewing and evaluating each plan under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-10 et seq. (4.3(a)).

Plan contents (4.3(c)1-14): cover page; evaluations; progress on prior goals; preferences/capabilities/needs; goals; measurable sequential objectives; method for each; team members and responsible persons; services with start dates, duration and frequency; barriers; guardianship review; meeting summary/addendum; attendance sign-off; authorization for approved individual expenses.
Procedures are built on normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning (2.2(a)2).
The 2023 text refers to the 'planning team'. Division Circular 52 (older) required the IHP within 30 days of admission and annual review. That is not in 10:44A, so confirm current DDD timelines.

policies.title: Implementation of Supports and Daily/Monthly Documentation
state_specifics: Plan and monthly documentation of progress are kept in the record (4.3(b)).
Train staff on all plans they implement (2.7(c)). Behavior support plans need specific training (2.7(d)5).
Use EVV for covered service hours and reconcile to the schedule.

policies.title: Changes in Supports and Services
state_specifics: Admission/change procedures must comply with 10:44A-4 (2.2(b)15). Confirm the operative 4.2 text before drafting notice timelines.
Changes in services must be reflected in the plan and communicated to the guardian, support coordinator and DDD.

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Community residence is defined as providing food, shelter, personal guidance and/or training and integration with the community (1.3).
Individuals get training and support to make choices (3.1(d)).
HCBS rule requires integration, opportunity to seek competitive integrated employment, and control of personal resources. Document each person's preferences and activities in the plan.
Siting not on or adjacent to public institution grounds supports integration (1.3).

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Record dates of discharge/transfer in the individual file (2.9(b)).
'Eviction' is defined in 1.3 (actual expulsion from the premises). Any involuntary discharge must follow the procedure in 10:44A-4. Confirm notice periods and appeal rights.
Coordinate with DDD, the support coordinator and the guardian. Move the individual's funds and records per policy.

policies.title: Shift Communication and Critical Information Log
state_specifics: Separate internal communication log, kept apart from individuals' records, documenting critical information and the licensee's follow-up (2.2(b)14).
Each entry is dated and signed with the staff member's full name.

'Critical information' includes unexpected behavioral outbursts, unexplained mood swings, PRN medication given, transportation problems, unexpected doctor/hospital visits, routine visits needing follow-up, reportable communicable diseases, and missed medical appointments (1.3).

policies.title: Medication Administration, Self-Medication and Staff Competency
state_specifics: Individuals self-administer to the extent possible as determined by the planning team (5.2(a)). Otherwise the licensee or designee assists and supervises (5.2(b)).
A record of all medication administered is kept (5.2(c)).
PRN labels must show interval, 24-hour maximum, stop date where appropriate and conditions for use. PRN doses are communicated to the oncoming shift (critical information).
Staff complete medication training and show competency before giving any medication, and annually thereafter (2.7(b)).
Manual must hold written medication procedures including self-medication (2.2(b)17).
2023 changes: APNs may prescribe; separate oral and other drops; for OTCs a manufacturer's label is acceptable (DHS 2/14/23 webinar). Confirm sections 5.3 to 5.6.

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: Feeding tube responsibilities are delegated to nursing personnel (2.7(d)1.i).
10:44A as read does not require a nurse consultant. If retained, define role (medication oversight, delegation, health plan review) in the manual.
General health care requirements (5.1) include routine and follow-up care. Confirm the section text before citing it.
Missed or unexpected medical visits are critical information (1.3).

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Staff working with individuals with seizure disorders, physical disabilities or other identified medical needs must receive specific training within 90 days of employment (2.7(d)3).
Specialized feeding techniques require training (2.7(d)1). Mobility device and safe transport training (2.7(d)2).
Each required specialized training must be completed by at least one person on every shift (2.8(b)).
Write individual protocols for seizures and choking in the plan and file.

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care (Danielle's Law)
state_specifics: Manual must require calling 9-1-1 for any life-threatening emergency, per Danielle's Law, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-5.1 et seq., and N.J.A.C. 10:42A (2.2(b)6).
All DSPs hold current first aid and CPR from an ECC-compliant entity (2.7(a)3-4).
Emergency coverage/on-call procedures required (2.2(b)7).
Unexpected doctor/hospital visits are critical information (1.3), and may also be reportable incidents.

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Treat as a reportable unusual incident (2.2(b)8) with an investigation procedure (2.2(b)9).
Record the date of discharge from services in the individual file (2.9(b)).
Notification of guardian, DDD and other authorities follows current DHS incident policy. Confirm timelines from the DDD incident reporting rules.
Feed review findings into CQI (2.2(b)22).

policies.title: Over-the-Counter Medications and First Aid Supplies
state_specifics: First aid kit includes a CPR mask and protective gloves (5.1(g)8-9, per DHS 2023 webinar).
OTC medication guidance and physician/APN statement on use are in 5.3. Confirm the current text before drafting.
OTC labels: manufacturer's label is acceptable (2023 amendment).

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support and Behavior Support Plans
state_specifics: 'Behavior support plan' means any individualized written planned action(s) taken before or after a target behavior to modify its frequency or intensity (1.3).

Staff working with individuals who require behavior support plans must be trained in implementing them within 90 days (2.7(d)5). Staff working with identified mental health needs receive specific training (2.7(d)4).
2023 amendment requires identification of all behavioral supports used (DHS webinar). Confirm section.
Consistent with least restriction (2.2(a)2).

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Restraint and Seclusion
state_specifics: Confirm the exact subchapter 5 section and allowed techniques before drafting. The restraint/behavioral-intervention section was not read.
Any restriction goes through the Human Rights Committee (3.1(e)) and the individual's plan.
Abuse includes wrongful physical, verbal or psychological abuse by a caregiver (1.3). Unapproved restraint or seclusion must be reported as such.
Limit to the least restrictive option (2.2(a)2).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Manual must contain a written statement expressly prohibiting abuse, neglect and exploitation, and a statement of the obligation to report each allegation under the statutes cited in 2.2(b)8.ii and Department policy.
DSP training on preventing abuse and neglect within 90 days (2.7(a)2).
Check the Central Registry of Offenders Against Individuals with DD (N.J.S.A. 30:6D-73 et seq.; N.J.A.C. 10:44D) and the DCF Child Abuse Registry (2.2(b)3, 2.2(b)20).
DDD number from research: 800-832-9173 (published for issues). Confirm current abuse/neglect hotline and reporting channel on the DHS site before printing.
Report promptly and protect the individual first. Preserve evidence.

policies.title: Reportable Incidents and Investigations
state_specifics: Procedure for reporting all unusual incidents (2.2(b)8) and a separate procedure for investigations (2.2(b)9).
Use the current DHS/DDD incident categories and timelines (not read here). Confirm and insert them.
Critical information (1.3) is communicated shift to shift.
Review incident patterns in CQI (2.2(b)22).

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: Missing-person events are treated as unusual incidents under 2.2(b)8. Confirm current DDD definitions and time thresholds.
Supervision follows each individual's needs (2.8(d)). Elopement risk goes in the plan.
Include immediate search steps, 9-1-1/police notification, and notification of guardian and DDD.

policies.title: Residential Environment, Capacity and Accessibility
state_specifics: License states each residence's location and maximum capacity (license provisions). Capacity: up to 16 per residence, up to 4 per supervised apartment (1.3).
Maintain documentation of Fire Official inspection, DCA registration and the local certificate (subchapter 6).
Do not acquire housing before consulting DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development (OPIA).
Match accessibility features to residents' needs. Confirm subchapter 6 section requirements (bedrooms, bathrooms, space).

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness, Evacuation and Fire Drills
state_specifics: Manual must include a plan for major emergencies requiring evacuation, such as fire or gas leak (2.2(b)5).
Fire safety is in subchapter 6 (6.1 to 6.17). Drill frequency, alarm and extinguisher requirements were not read, so confirm them.
Obtain Fire Official inspection documentation and DCA registration where required.
Emergency coverage and on-call procedures (2.2(b)7). Staff must be on site whenever an individual is present (2.8(d)).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Reportable communicable diseases are critical information (1.3).
Staff TB screening (2.4): Mantoux or IGRA within one year before or upon starting work.
Protective gloves and CPR mask belong in the first aid kit (5.1(g)8-9, 2023).
2023 amendment: thaw food in refrigerator.
OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard applies to employees with exposure. Include an exposure control plan.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Staff supporting specialized feeding must be trained (2.7(d)1). Feeding tube duties are delegated to nursing (2.7(d)1.i).
Confirm the food/nutrition section of subchapter 5 (meal frequency, menus, modified diets) before drafting.
Food access respects HCBS settings expectations.

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Staff working with mobility devices must be trained in mobility procedures and safe use of devices, including those needed for transport (2.7(d)2).
Problems with transportation are critical information (1.3).
DDD-approved providers run driver abstract checks for staff who transport (per research). The rule citation was not verified.
Confirm any subchapter 5 vehicle rule before citing.

policies.title: Temperature and Utility Emergencies
state_specifics: Manual must address emergencies where evacuation may not be required, such as indoor air temperature below 68F or above 82F for four consecutive hours (2.2(b)5.i).
Define who decides, how individuals are relocated or protected, and how DDD and the Office of Licensing are notified.

policies.title: Staff Coverage, Two-Week Schedule and In-Charge Designation
state_specifics: Written schedule for at least two weeks at each residence, full staff names, on-site coverage per the program description (2.8(a)).
Employee in charge designated for each shift.
Staff on site whenever any individual is present, based on supervision needs (2.8(d)). Supervised apartment office/residence sited for response time (2.8(e)).

No numeric ratio or awake-overnight rule was found in 10:44A (the 1:3 awake ratio is in 10:44C and does not apply). Set overnight coverage from the program description and each individual's plan, and confirm with the Office of Licensing.
Keep EVV records aligned with the schedule.

policies.title: Background Checks, Central Registry and Child Abuse Registry
state_specifics: Agency head: no pay or contract until criminal history clearance (FBI and NJ State Police records) under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-63 through 69. Owners/licensee also checked if different (1.4(b)).
Manual must include a procedure for Central Registry compliance (2.2(b)3) and for ensuring no employee is on the DCF Child Abuse Registry (2.2(b)20).
All employees who may contact individuals must comply with screening (2.4(d), per provider-hosted copy). Confirm that subsection.
Fingerprinting mechanics and timelines were not verified, so ask the Office of Licensing.

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Qualifications, Orientation and Basic Training
state_specifics: DSP minimums: age 18+, HS diploma or equivalent (2.5(c)). Able to communicate with the individuals served (2.5(d)). Able to provide required assistance (2.5(e)).
New Employee Orientation Checklist covering at least 2.6(a)1-8 (2.2(b)4). Confirm those eight items from 2.6.
Within 90 days: DDD Shifting Expectations, preventing abuse and neglect, first aid and CPR with valid ECC-compliant certificates (2.7(a)).
Training in all job-relevant policies not covered in orientation (2.7(c)).
Training records at the administrative office: curriculum/plan, dated trainer and trainee signatures, Division-required results (2.7(e)).

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Direct service staff take a Mantoux tuberculin skin test (5 TU PPD) or an IGRA blood test within one year before or upon beginning work. Written results go to the licensee.
Handling of a previous positive result is addressed in the rule. Read it and add it.
2005 text required annual repeat testing, so confirm whether the current text still does.
Time frame for staff physicals was changed in the 2023 amendments (DHS webinar). Confirm the current requirement.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Inspectors review staff files, schedules, credentials and background checks (OPIA).
File holds application, education proof, background/registry clearances, TB documentation, CDS testing results, training certificates (first aid, CPR, DDD basic), and medication competency (annual).
Licensee verifies professional credentials required by law (2.5(f)).
Training records are kept at the administrative office (2.7(e)).
Job descriptions for each table-of-organization position are reviewed by DDD (1.4(i)2).

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Prohibit abuse, neglect and exploitation in writing (2.2(b)8.i). Exploitation includes using an individual or their resources for another's profit or advantage (1.3).
No staff handling individual funds outside the fund procedure (2.2(b)10).
Staff must be able to communicate with individuals and respect their rights (2.5(d), 3.1(c)).
Gifts, loans, social media, dual relationships, and discipline for violations are agency policy and not specified in 10:44A.

policies.title: Employee Controlled Dangerous Substance Testing
state_specifics: Written procedures for testing employees for controlled dangerous substances in accordance with N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 (2.2(b)18).
Research indicates DDD-approved providers conduct pre-employment and random testing. Confirm the current testing standard from the statute.

policies.title: Emergency Coverage and On-Call Procedures
state_specifics: Required manual content (2.2(b)7).
When no individuals are present, staff need not be on site, but trained, paid agency staff familiar with the individuals must be available for emergencies (2.8(c)).
Publish an on-call roster and how it is reached.

policies.title: Specialized Training and Qualified Trainers
state_specifics: Specialized training identified by the Department, placing agency or licensee must be completed within 90 days of employment (2.7(d)).
At least one person on each shift must have each required specialized training for that site (2.8(b)).
Training under 2.7(c) is delivered by a qualified trainer (2.7(g)). 2023 amendments added the 'qualified trainer' concept (DHS webinar).

policies.title: Temporary Agency Staff and In-Charge Restrictions
state_specifics: Temporary employment agency staff may not be designated or used as 'in-charge' unless all 2.7 training is complete and a written policy states the licensee assumes responsibility and liability for their actions (2.8(a)2.i).

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
state_specifics: An individual file is kept for each individual (2.9(a)). Group home/supervised apartment files stay at the residence (2.9(b)).
Contents include full name, DOB, sex, Social Security/Medicaid numbers, and dates of admission, readmission, transfer or discharge. Add other contents after reading the rest of 2.9.
Plan and monthly progress documentation belong in the record (4.3(b)). Financial records are covered by 2.10.
The state retention period was not found in the sections read, so confirm it. Federal minimums are 6 years under HIPAA documentation rules.
Keep shift communication logs separate from individual records (2.2(b)14).

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Provide files, reports or records to the Department on request. Refusal is grounds for adverse action.
Unusual incident reports and abuse/neglect allegations per 2.2(b)8.
Annual financial statement audit if claiming $350,000+ combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement. Follows GAAS.
Fiscal Sustainability Report due 120 days after state fiscal year end (about October 30).
CPA examination of financial status and Management Letters for two fiscal years are required at application (1.4(c)1.x).
Report changes in ownership, governance, agency head and penalties or fines relevant to program safety (1.4(c)1.ix). Confirm change-notice rules.
